text:
alex: Heads up — Feb invoice shows a weird 'ReservedCapacityAdjustment' credit (~-$42,000) applied in asia-east1 but our GPU (A100/T4) line items in APAC are still billed at full rate. Not what we expected.
maria: :eyes: I noticed GPUs looked high in the screenshot sent this morning. Did credits get targeted to wrong SKU or region?
jyoti: My first pass: reservation credits appear to have been matched to standard compute vCPU SKUs instead of accelerator SKUs. Possibly due to a recent reservation family rename when we scaled the fleet.
alex: That would explain it. We recently migrated some dedicated pools from n1-standard -> n2-highcpu and then reclassified GPU attachments. Could be the mapping rule.
samir: Can someone paste the invoice line snippet? I want to see the exact descriptions the cloud provider used.
maria: Pasting the relevant lines from the invoice CSV (redacted):

`2026-02-28, asia-east1, n2-highcpu-8+A100, GPU-Hour, 480, $3.20, $1536.00`
`2026-02-28, asia-east1, ReservedCapacityAdjustment, -1, -$42000.00, CREDIT`
`2026-02-28, asia-east1, n2-highcpu-8, vCPU-Hour, 3840, $0.02, $76.80`
`2026-02-28, asia-east1, GPU-Support-Surcharge, 1, $1200.00`

jyoti: The ReservedCapacityAdjustment has no SKU tag linking to accelerators. Looks like the provider applied one big reservation credit to the account without SKU granularity.
billing-bot: Export generated: /billing/exports/2051234567-apac-resv-adjustment.csv (CSV includes line-item ids and invoice ids)
finance-ops: @samir filing FIN-742 with billing support, attaching the CSV and the CE query results.
samir: Thanks. Can someone run a cost-explorer split by "UsageType" + "ResourceTag:reserved-pool" and share numbers? I want to see if credits were consumed by non-accelerator usage.
jyoti: Ran quick CE query:
`aws ce get-cost-and-usage --time-period Start=2026-02-01,End=2026-02-28 --granularity MONTHLY --metrics UnblendedCost --group-by Type=DIMENSION,Key=USAGE_TYPE`
Result (summary): vCPU usage consumed $37k of the reservation credit, GPU usage consumed $5.5k. Remainder unmatched.
maria: So the credit principally offset vCPU, leaving GPUs mostly billed. That leads to an effective double-hit: we lost GPU credits and still paid for vCPU usage not intended for this reservation.
alex: Is this from our committed-reservation product (reserved capacity for GPUs) or from a general commitment pool? Which SKU did we purchase against?
finance-ops: Contract shows we purchased a "Dedicated Accelerator Commitment" scoped to asia-east1 (SKU: ACC-DED-A100-2026). Billing description mismatch: invoice labels it as ReservedCapacityAdjustment without SKU tag.
samir: Action plan:
1) FIN-742 opened with provider support (assigned to @samir)
2) Attach CSV and CE export, request reallocation of the reservation credit to accelerator SKUs or a manual credit.
3) Short-term: set a billing rule to tag all accelerator attachments with "accelerator-reservation" to force matching (devops change).
4) Estimate impact and hold next payroll transfer if needed (finance sign-off). 

samir: I'm pinging provider rep now. Provider response ETA 48 hours.
maria: Devops note: we're adding an invariant in the autoscale job that preserves the reservation family label when instance families change. PR queued.
jyoti: Also checking whether support surcharge line `GPU-Support-Surcharge` appears duplicated vs prior months.
alex: Estimate impact if not resolved: additional ~$25k net overcharge (we get some of the $42k back as vCPU credit but still pay GPUs). Need to track exposure.
finance-ops: Recording tentative write-down for March forecasts until provider confirms.
billing-bot: Support ticket FIN-742 created: https://billing.provider/requests/FIN-742 (ops:attached csv)
samir: Will update once provider responds. If they don't reallocate, we'll need a manual credit and a call with account manager.
alex: Thanks all. Keep threads short in this channel — if you need deeper debugging, move to #eng-billing and tag me. :thumbsup:
maria: I'll follow up with the PR link and the CE exports in the ticket.
jyoti: Adding a postmortem stub to docs once resolved.
samir: Closing loop — next update here in ~48h or sooner.
